history.summary: South-facing (Dakshinamukhi) Hanuman shrine in the old market quarter of Naya Ganj / Agrasen Market, near Delhi Gate, standing in the middle of the market road on the historic 'Chopla' (communal gathering place). Built in Vikram Samvat 1981 (AD 1924) by Lala Raghuchir Saran Kabuliwala in memory of his father Lala Ramjidas Kabuli; renovated in 2005 (Vasant Panchami, VS 2061) by the founder's family. Houses an ancient well still in use, a Rama parivar shrine and a Shiva linga.

name: Chopla Hanuman Mandir
town_description: Industrial city in western Uttar Pradesh, part of the National Capital Region on the Delhi–Meerut corridor; a major rail and road hub with Ghaziabad Junction, Delhi Metro Red Line and the RRTS linking it to Delhi.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, ~40 km (verify)
travel.road: Agrasen Market, Naya Ganj, near Delhi Gate (Dasna Gate area); nearest metro Shaheed Sthal (New Bus Adda)

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM – 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM – 10:00 PM (per the temple listing; verify)
